verdict_reason: The fit is Facco et al.'s five-step Two-NN algorithm verbatim: mu_i = r2/r1; F_emp(mu_sigma(i)) = i/N (one-based, exactly as the paper's step 4 states and as the authors' own DADApy package implements it - `y = -np.log(1 - np.arange(1, n_eff+1)/N)`, which I fetched and read); discard the top 10% of mu; least-squares line through the origin of (log mu, -log(1-F_emp)). It reproduces THREE independent published Fig. 1 anchors at N=2500 with the 10% discard: the 14-D hypercube analysed with periodic boundary conditions gives 13.83 over 5 reps against a published 13.91 (-0.56%), the Swiss roll gives 1.952 against 2.01 (-2.89%), and the Cauchy d=20 cloud gives 22.67 against 22.16 (+2.30%). No published RNG seed exists, so per-rep scatter is the limiting factor, not the estimator.
comparable_reason: In the configuration the study runs (layerwise=true), the mean-over-layers ID is a width proxy: over 61 archived models Spearman +0.701 with d_model, +0.550 with n_layers, +0.681 with log(params), +0.121 with vocab; max-over-layers +0.646 / +0.598 / +0.352 / +0.676. The whole 61-model zoo spans only 6.27-9.05 in mean layer ID, so almost all of the between-model variance is that width term. Two-NN is distance-based and ambient-dimension invariant in principle, so this is not arithmetic - but the estimator ALSO truncates severely and dimension-dependently at finite N, which biases wide models differently. A log(d_model) divisor would work if one were emitted: mean-over-layers / log(d_model) has rho -0.027 with d_model, +0.060 with n_layers. As reported, the raw value is not cross-model valid.
normalized_variant: intrinsic_dimension_scalenorm (= intrinsic_dimension / log(d_model); NORMALIZERS in src/blme/normalization.py)
github_reason: I fetched DADApy's dadapy/id_estimation.py, the package maintained by the Facco/d'Errico/Laio group, and it uses `y = -np.log(1 - np.arange(1, n_eff + 1) / N)` with `curve_fit(lambda x,m: m*x, ...)` - one-based empirical CDF, origin fit, exactly BLME's convention. I also ran the installed scikit-dimension 0.3.4 skdim.id.TwoNN head-to-head on identical clouds: BLME is consistently ABOVE it by +18.2% / +3.3% / +0.33% / +0.065% at N = 20 / 100 / 1000 / 5000 (identical to 4 significant figures across d = 2, 5, 10), because skdim uses `Femp = np.arange(int(N*(1-discard)))/N` - ZERO-based. So BLME agrees with the paper and with the authors' package, and skdim is the deviant one. PARTIAL because I did not build the authors' C++ efacco/TWO-NN release.
paper_reason: Facco et al. 2017, Fig. 1 and the surrounding text, N=2500 with the top 10% of mu discarded: hypercube d=14 analysed with periodic boundary conditions -> 13.91, Swiss roll -> 2.01, Cauchy d=20 -> 22.16. Feeding BLME's _twonn_linear_fit the toroidal-distance (r1, r2) of five fresh 2500-point 14-cubes gives 13.868 / 14.065 / 13.232 / 13.927 / 14.065, mean 13.8316, relative error -0.56% (best rep 0.12%). Five Swiss rolls give mean 1.9519, -2.89%. Three Cauchy d=20 clouds give 23.05 / 22.00 / 22.96, mean 22.67, +2.30%.
confounds_reason: Over 61 archived models, intrinsic_dim mean-over-layers has rho +0.701 with d_model (and +0.681 with log params); max-over-layers +0.646 / +0.676. The mechanism is not the estimator's ambient dimension (Two-NN uses only distance ratios) but finite-N truncation, which is itself dimension-dependent: on isotropic Gaussians at fixed N the reported ID rises monotonically with the true dimension but saturates well below it, so wider models with higher true local dimension are compressed differently from narrow ones. Dividing by log(d_model) removes the association almost exactly (rho -0.027), which is direct evidence the confound is a d_model-scaled ceiling rather than signal.
defects: PROVENANCE (task_metadata.py): 'Bit-identical to skdim _TwoNN fit on analytic Pareto samples' is FALSE. Measured deviation vs skdim 0.3.4 on identical clouds: +18.2% (N=20), +3.3% (N=100), +0.33% (N=1000), +0.065% (N=5000), from BLME's one-based empirical CDF against skdim's zero-based one. BLME is the CORRECT one (it matches Facco step 4 and the authors' DADApy) - the claim should say so instead of claiming skdim parity.

CODE: the config key is dead. intrinsic_dim.py:83 reads self.config.get('_meta_sample_size', None), so a recipe setting `sample_size` is silently ignored. VERIFIED on gpt2: config sample_size=100 -> realized N = 50257 (the whole vocabulary); config _meta_sample_size=100 -> realized N = 100. The internal-looking _meta_ key is the only one that works.

CODE: exact duplicates are removed AFTER the kNN search (the `r1 > 0` filter at intrinsic_dim.py:116), so duplicates corrupt their NEIGHBOURS' r1/r2 as well as their own. VERIFIED: a 200-point 2-D cloud returns 1.9483; duplicating every point returns NaN; deduplicating first returns 1.9483 again. DADApy calls remove_zero_dists on the distance array before forming mus.
CODE: `mus = mus[mus > 1.0]` silently drops the mu == 1 population as well as numerical noise. Those are legitimate (0,0) points on the regression line.

CONFIG: the package default layerwise=false applies Two-NN to the whole static input-embedding table, which is not the Ansuini per-layer activation protocol the docstring cites. The study recipe overrides to layerwise=true, so the published numbers are the per-layer version - but a user running BLME's defaults gets a different quantity under the same key.

CODE: the paper defines the 'relevant' ID for real data by subsampling over N and locating a plateau in d(N). The task emits a single full-sample slope with no plateau test, no uncertainty and no failure mode, while the finite-N truncation is large and dimension-dependent.
fix: Correct the metadata to 'follows Facco step 4's one-based empirical CDF, matching the authors' DADApy; deviates from scikit-dimension's zero-based convention by ~1/N (+0.33% at N=1000)'. Restore the `sample_size` config lookup and keep `_meta_sample_size` as output only. Deduplicate the coordinate matrix BEFORE the kNN search and report the number removed. Rename the layerwise=false path so it reads as the input-embedding table. Add Facco-style repeated subsampling with a d(N) plateau check and an uncertainty. For cross-model use, emit an explicitly named `intrinsic_dimension_over_logd` twin - I measured that it takes rho with d_model from +0.701 to -0.027 - rather than leaving the raw value to a regression. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): the registered twin intrinsic_dimension/log(d_model) is RED on three counts. (1) It never fires in the study configuration -- configs/tasks.yaml sets layerwise:true, that path emits only lid_layer_* and lid_trend, and `intrinsic_dimension` is absent from all 66 archived envelopes; the +0.701 -> -0.027 figure recorded in normalization.py was measured on the mean-over-layers ID, a different key. (2) In the shipped default (layerwise:false) the key is the Two-NN ID of the INPUT EMBEDDING table at N = vocab_size, and over 13 freshly run models it tracks vocabulary, not width: rho(vocab) = +0.940 (p = 2e-06) against rho(d_model) = +0.014, and dividing by log(d_model) leaves rho(vocab) at +0.940 untouched while pushing rho(n_layers) from -0.253 to -0.452. (That panel has only four distinct vocabulary sizes, so part of the +0.94 is a family contrast -- but the divisor is a function of d alone and cannot address either reading.) The protocol is also not model-neutral: recomputing the same estimator with N held at 20000 instead of |V| moves the value by +11% to +67% and does so model-specifically (SmolLM2-135M 1.11x, gpt2 1.22x, pythia-160m 1.66x, pythia-70m 1.67x over 9 models), so each model is measured at its own sample size. (3) The stated mechanism is false: Two-NN is EXACTLY invariant to isometric embedding (9.6296 at ambient d = 64/128/.../4096, bit-identical), and in the one case where a width term does exist -- an isotropic cloud at fixed N -- the estimate grows as d^+0.55 (power-law fit R2 = 0.9992) rather than as log d (R2 = 0.9190). Remove the registration.
